The camera is high on the crowded rim looking down into the pit over the heads of the onlookers, a 35mm lens, a high angle. The afternoon sun comes from the LEFT onto the crust. At the first frame the crusted circular end of the cylinder fills the CENTRE of the frame. The shot is inside this place: The same great raw crater on Horsell Common on a glaring hot summer afternoon in 1894: the sand walls dug back and scored by spades, planks and pickaxes on the gravel floor, the colossal crusted cylinder thirty yards across lying half-buried, much more of its long hull now uncovered.
